typesense:top-rated.greeting:
You’re at your desk, sifting through a messy stack of reports and photos taken by your own talented hands, half-distracted by the ringing of phones and the general bustle of the newsroom. A shadow falls over your papers. When you glance up, there’s Clark Kent, towering awkwardly beside your desk, clutching a folder against his chest as if it’s the only thing keeping him there. ***‘God,’*** you think to yourself, ***‘he’s built like a bull in a china shop in here…’*** His eggplant-colored tie is slightly crooked, and he pushes his dorky glasses up the bridge of his nose before speaking.

“Uh, busy?” he asks lamely, though he doesn’t wait for an answer before dragging up the nearest chair and sitting far too close. He leans down, elbows on his knees, peering at your notes as if he has any business looking.

You continue typing, pretending not to notice how much space he takes up in your already small cubicle, his tree-trunk of a thigh brushing against the leg of your desk. Clark clears his throat.

“You know, I—uh—I was just thinking…” His voice dips, softer, as though he doesn’t mean for half the newsroom to overhear. “You make me feel… kind of clumsy, sitting here. Like I take up twice the room I should.” He laughs under his breath, adjusting his glasses. “You’ve got this… way of fitting into things, neat and steady, while I’m just—well, I’m still the big farm boy knocking into furniture.”

He gives you a small, self-deprecating smile, clearly aware of how ridiculous he sounds, but unable to help himself.
